summary: Regime read: Potential pivot → tightening. Of the weighted evidence, 68% points tightening, 22% mixed, and 10% easing. Inflation is strongly tightening (Inflation is above target and rising; the US labor market is stronger than expected due to excessive stimulus.). Fed communications are strongly tightening (The Fed adopted a hawkish tone in its post-meeting policy statement, with nine members projecting at least one hike in 2026 and futures markets fully pricing in a rate hike in October.). Employment is leaning tightening and market pricing is strongly tightening.
what_would_change_the_call: A second consecutive upside inflation surprise.
Front-end (2Y) yields rising materially further over the intermeeting window.
A Fed official explicitly pushing back against near-term cuts.
Fed funds futures repricing from 'fewer cuts' toward outright hikes.

checklist.text: Fed communications explicitly de-emphasize further easing
Fed emphasizes inflation upside risks over labor weakness
Market pricing removes expected cuts or starts pricing hikes
2Y yields rise materially over the intermeeting window
Inflation data surprises to the upside
Employment remains firm enough to reduce pressure for cuts
SPY/TLT color and rate-market behavior confirm the macro read

scoring.method: weighted vote-share over source direction (no magnitude averaging)

sources.title: US 10 Year Treasury Note Yield - Quote - Chart
sources.evidence_text: Markets are pricing in an 80% chance of a Fed rate hike in December following last week's hawkish pause, while the probability of a September increase stands at around 63%.
sources.why_it_matters: High market-implied probabilities for December and September hikes reinforce a tightening trajectory, pressuring the Fed to align its reaction function with market expectations.

sources.title: June US Jobs Report: 147,000 Rise in Payrolls, Stronger Than Expected
sources.evidence_text: Total nonfarm payrolls rose by 147,000 in June, surpassing the forecast of 115,000, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%.
sources.why_it_matters: Stronger-than-expected job growth and a lower unemployment rate signal robust labor demand, reducing the likelihood of immediate Fed rate cuts.

sources.title: US labor market adds 147,000 jobs in June while unemployment falls to 4.1%
sources.evidence_text: Following the report, expectations for a July rate reduction diminished significantly, with CME FedWatch showing only a 5% likelihood of a cut.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing has rapidly adjusted to reflect a tighter Fed stance due to resilient labor data, directly impacting the probability of future easing.

sources.title: United States Employment Rate
sources.evidence_text: The US Employment Rate increased to 59.20% in May from 59.10% in April 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A marginal increase in the employment rate suggests stability rather than a significant shift in labor market dynamics requiring immediate policy action.

sources.title: Initial Claims (ICSA) | FRED | St. Louis Fed
sources.evidence_text: FRED data shows Initial Claims trending downward to 215,000 by June 20, 2026, reflecting recent labor market improvement.
sources.why_it_matters: Trend data confirms declining claims, supporting labor stability and reducing urgency for Fed cuts, though historical volatility remains a factor.

sources.title: 2026 US Economics Outlook: Emerging From Policy Uncertainty
sources.evidence_text: We expect 25bp rate cuts in December, January, and April as the Fed takes its policy stance close to neutral.
sources.why_it_matters: Morgan Stanley's forecast of modest rate cuts aligns with a neutral policy stance, indicating limited pressure for significant easing or tightening.

sources.title: June 2026 – U.S. Economic Snapshot
sources.evidence_text: Year-over-year inflation rose from 3.78% to 4.17%, and core PCE inflation shot up from 3.05% to 3.91% (month-over-month, annualized).
sources.why_it_matters: The sharp increase in core PCE, the Fed's preferred measure, strongly supports a tightening reaction function.

sources.title: June FOMC recap—It’s task force time | Franklin Templeton
sources.evidence_text: Nine of the 18 participants now see at least one rate hike before the end of 2026, and median estimates for 2026 core PCE inflation were revised substantially higher to 3.3%.
sources.why_it_matters: The substantial upward revision to inflation forecasts and the majority of participants expecting a hike confirm the Fed's reaction function is pivoting to tightening to counter inflationary pressures.

sources.title: Fed rate cut by...? Predictions & Odds 2026
sources.evidence_text: Persistent inflation has emerged as the dominant force shaping expectations for Federal Reserve policy, with the May 2026 CPI rising 4.2% year-over-year.
sources.why_it_matters: High CPI data and persistent inflation in market expectations reinforce a tightening bias, reducing the probability of rate cuts in the Fed's reaction function.

sources.title: Fed Shifts to Hawkish Tune, But Keeps Rates Steady
sources.evidence_text: The Fed adopted a hawkish tone in its post-meeting policy statement, with nine members projecting at least one hike in 2026 and futures markets fully pricing in a rate hike in October.
sources.why_it_matters: Hawkish Fed communications and internal projections shift the reaction function toward tightening by reinforcing inflation concerns and reducing cut expectations.

sources.title: 30 Day Federal Funds Futures Overview - CME Group
sources.evidence_text: Fed Fund futures provide a gauge of market expectations about the Fed’s action at future FOMC meetings, with current prices indicating upward pressure on rates.
sources.why_it_matters: Futures prices serve as a real-time indicator of market sentiment, influencing the Fed’s reaction function by signaling tightening expectations.

sources.title: Market Probability Tracker - Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta
sources.evidence_text: The Market Probability Tracker estimates probability distributions implied by Chicago Mercantile Exchange options prices, showing elevated odds of higher fed funds rates.
sources.why_it_matters: Market-implied probabilities from SOFR options reinforce tightening signals, informing the Fed’s reaction function by highlighting upward rate pressure.

sources.title: Fed Rate Monitor Tool - Investing.com
sources.evidence_text: The fed watch tool displays a forecast estimation for fed hikes or cuts, with current data showing a 67.9% probability of a rate hike at the next FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Investing.com’s Fed Rate Monitor reinforces tightening signals by quantifying market expectations for hikes, influencing the Fed’s reaction function.

sources.title: US Treasury yields jump as Fed projections lift rate hike bets for 2026
sources.evidence_text: The yield on the policy-sensitive two-year Treasury note rose 11 basis points to 4.16% following the Fed decision, with the dollar also gaining.
sources.why_it_matters: The sharp rise in the 2-year yield signals market expectations of future rate hikes, directly contradicting easing and supporting a tightening bias in the Fed reaction function.
